title: In-Situ 4D STEM: Capturing 5D Insights into Material Dynamics in Liquid
content: Four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D STEM) is a powerful and versatile family of techniques that has rapidly gained popularity and is now being used to investigate a wide range of materials under various conditions [1]. The widespread adoption of in-situ Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) has been facilitated by the proliferation of advanced in-situ holders, enabling the application of diverse stimuli. In-situ 4D STEM has arisen at the confluence of these two trends, enabling the capture of 4D STEM data cubes at discrete points during an experiment or even continuously over time to generate 5D datasets. This approach provides valuable insights into the structure and dynamics of materials at the nanoscale.
